```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`FINNmodelNBINetherlands` ships a fitted [FINN](https://github.com/FINNverse/FINN)
forest model for the Netherlands: 14 tree taxa (species, or the genus where the
NBI records only the genus; no "other" class), calibrated to the tree-by-tree
remeasurement of the permanent plots of the Dutch national forest inventory
(NBI) on stands where these 14 taxa hold more than 98 % of the basal area
(model card in the [FINN-zoo](https://finnverse.github.io/FINN-zoo/models.html)).
The package downloads the released parameters once, rebuilds the model with the
installed FINN (>= 0.2.0) and simulates forest dynamics for sites you describe
by two WorldClim 2.1 climate normals and a harvest dial.

The chunks are not evaluated when the package is built: loading the model
downloads the released parameters once and needs a torch backend. Run them
after installing the release:

```{r install}
remotes::install_github("FINNverse/FINN@0848b60")                   # FINN 0.2.0, the version the model was fitted with
remotes::install_github("FINNverse/FINN-model-NBI-Netherlands@v0.1.0")
library(FINNmodelNBINetherlands)
library(FINN)
library(data.table)
torch::torch_set_num_threads(1L)   # pinned: one thread, the setting the model was fitted and validated with
```

Threads and batch size are pinned: one torch thread, and every
`simulate_model()` call below passes `batchsize = 100L` (sites per simulation
batch, the value pinned in `model_info()`). A different batchsize changes the
random draws but not the model (the batch size only changes how the stochastic
draws of recruit numbers and patch-level mortality are consumed); the same
seed, thread count and batch size reproduce a run exactly. Use
`FINN::FINN.seed()` before a run.

## What the model needs

- `env`: one row per site and year with `siteID`, `year` (1, 2, ...), `tavg_c`
  (annual mean temperature, degC, WorldClim 2.1 bio1), `prec_mm` (annual
  precipitation, mm, bio12), in natural units (the model standardises
  internally with the constants it learned), and `harvest` (0 or 1): the
  management dial of the mortality process. `harvest = 1` means the stand is
  harvested as the inventory's harvested plots were (on those, 22 % of the
  trees were felled over an interval of 4-12 years), `harvest = 0` means no
  harvest activity; the simulated "mortality" is total stem loss, felling
  included, in both cases. See `inst/model/covariates.csv` for how to derive
  the covariates for new sites. The calibration range is the Dutch climate
  (roughly 9-10.5 degC, 710-940 mm); outside it the model extrapolates.
- optionally an initial stand: a table of cohorts (`siteID`, `patchID`,
  `species`, `dbh` in cm, `trees`) turned into a `CohortMat` with
  `FINN::makeInitCohorts()`. The species index is `species_table()`; `trees`
  counts stems on one patch of **0.1257 ha** (the 20 m NBI circle), the patch
  size the model was fitted with. Without an initial stand the simulation
  starts from bare ground.

```{r species}
model_info()          # release tag, parameter file, sha256, FINN commit, patch settings
head(species_table()) # species index -> name, NBI code, Dutch name
```

## Bare-ground succession at two climates

```{r bare}
env <- CJ(siteID = 1:2, year = 1:300)
env[, tavg_c  := c(9.3, 10.2)[siteID]]      # a cooler north-eastern and a warmer southern site
env[, prec_mm := c(830, 770)[siteID]]
env[, harvest := 0L]                        # no harvest: the free run

FINN.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_model(env, init_cohort = NULL, patches = 20L, batchsize = 100L)   # 20 patches of 0.1257 ha per site
out <- as.data.table(sim$wide$site)
out <- merge(out, species_table()[, c("species", "species_name")], by = "species")
out[, ba_ha := ba / 0.1257]             # basal area per hectare
stand <- out[, .(ba_ha = sum(ba_ha)), by = .(siteID, year)]
plot(stand[siteID == 1, .(year, ba_ha)], type = "l", ylim = c(0, 60), ylab = "basal area (m2/ha)")
lines(stand[siteID == 2, .(year, ba_ha)], col = "red")
```

## Simulating from a synthetic stand

The stand below is an example, not an NBI plot (the inventory data are not
redistributed with this package): a Scots pine stand with oak and birch
understorey on the sandy soils of the Veluwe.

```{r stand}
init <- data.table(siteID = 1L, patchID = 1L,
                   species = c(9L, 12L, 3L),       # Pinus sylvestris, Quercus robur/petraea, Betula (see species_table())
                   dbh     = c(32, 14, 10),        # cm
                   trees   = c(45, 30, 25))        # stems on the 0.1257 ha patch
init_cohort <- makeInitCohorts(init, Nspecies = nrow(species_table()))
env <- data.table(siteID = 1L, year = 1:50, tavg_c = 10.0, prec_mm = 830, harvest = 0L)
FINN.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_model(env, init_cohort = init_cohort, patches = 1L, batchsize = 100L)
as.data.table(sim$wide$site)[year == 50 & trees > 0]

## the same stand under the harvest regime of the inventory's harvested plots
env_h <- copy(env)[, harvest := 1L]
FINN.seed(1)
sim_h <- simulate_model(env_h, init_cohort = init_cohort, patches = 1L, batchsize = 100L)
as.data.table(sim_h$wide$site)[year == 50 & trees > 0]
```

## Notes

- The mortality process was fitted to total stem loss, natural death and
  felling together (they cannot be separated tree by tree in the NBI and the
  Dutch forest is managed throughout), with the `harvest` dial as the only
  management information; `harvest = 0` is therefore not "unmanaged forest"
  but "no harvest recorded in the interval". Plots that lost half or more of
  their basal area between the visits (clearcuts) were not used.
- The model was calibrated on stands where the 14 taxa hold > 98 % of the
  basal area at the start of an interval (77.6 % of the inventory's plot
  pairs); its holdout skill falls on stands where other species gain ground.
  Free (bare-ground) runs end up dominated by Douglas fir, beech, larch, red
  oak, Acer and Salix at 46-55 m2/ha; Scots pine, oak and birch hardly
  establish. Use the model for projections from an observed stand over one to
  a few decades, not as a succession model.
- Outputs per patch: `ba` m2, `trees` stems, `dbh` cm (species mean), `growth`
  relative dbh increment per year, `mort` annual loss probability, `reg` and
  `r_mean_ha` recruits (per patch and per ha and year; recruits enter at 5.9 cm
  dbh, the NBI tally threshold being 5 cm).
- FINN's simulated mortality has a floor of 0.01 per annual step
  (FINNverse/FINN#51); species with a fitted loss rate below 1 % per year are
  simulated at the floor, which the fit did not see. With the stem-loss target
  of this model (turnover incl. felling, 10 % per year on average) the floor
  rarely binds.
- The weights are released as GitHub release assets of this repository: the
  name-matched parameter dump `parameters.pt` (a named list of tensors, env
  networks and env standardisation included) that `load_model()` downloads,
  checks against the sha256 in `model_info()` and copies into a freshly built
  model, and the whole fitted module `model.pt` for `torch::torch_load()`.
  The calibration script asserts that the rebuilt model reproduces the fitted
  one bit for bit. The fit used `weights = "auto"` (baseline-scaled losses, no
  numeric weight vector, so `weight_scale` is moot).
